description:
SpaceGuard Africa is a multidisciplinary team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to develop an innovative space technology solution that addresses climate resilience and environmental challenges in Africa.
Our team is passionate about Artificial Intelligence (AI), IoT, embedded systems, software development, data science, climate innovation, and Earth observation. We are committed to building a practical prototype that demonstrates how space technology can support communities through intelligent environmental monitoring and data-driven decision support.
We believe in teamwork, creativity, and solving real-world challenges using science and technology. We welcome collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovative thinking throughout the hackathon.
summary:
SpaceGuard Africa is an environmental intelligence and disaster early-warning platform developed to monitor environmental changes and support climate resilience across Africa, starting with The Gambia. The project integrates NASA Earth observation and climate datasets with real-time measurements from a physical environmental monitoring station in Fajara, equipped with an Arduino MKR WiFi 1010, temperature and humidity, soil moisture, rain and water sensors.

By combining satellite-based observations with ground-level measurements, the platform aims to analyse environmental trends, identify changing conditions and provide AI-supported insights into potential drought and flood risks. Its interactive dashboard presents environmental information for different locations, distinguishing areas with physical monitoring stations from those monitored using NASA data.

SpaceGuard Africa addresses the Environmental Trend Analysis challenge by transforming scientific and sensor data into accessible, location-specific environmental intelligence. It is important because timely environmental information can help communities, researchers and decision-makers better understand climate patterns, strengthen disaster preparedness and make more informed decisions to protect livelihoods and infrastructure.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

SpaceGuard Africa is an environmental intelligence and disaster early-warning platform designed to monitor environmental changes, analyse climate trends and support disaster preparedness across Africa, beginning with The Gambia.

The platform combines two major sources of environmental information: NASA Earth observation and climate datasets, and real-time measurements collected from a physical environmental monitoring station located in Fajara, The Gambia.

The physical station uses an Arduino MKR WiFi 1010 connected to environmental sensors, including a DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, a capacitive soil moisture sensor, a rain sensor and a water-level sensor. The microcontroller collects measurements and transmits them through Wi-Fi to our cloud-based backend, where they can be accessed by the SpaceGuard Africa dashboard.

Alongside the physical measurements, the platform uses NASA environmental datasets to examine variables such as precipitation, temperature, relative humidity and wind speed. These datasets support the analysis of historical and regional environmental trends, including comparisons between locations with and without physical monitoring stations.

The platform brings these different sources together to provide a broader understanding of environmental conditions. Its AI-supported analysis is intended to help interpret environmental information and identify potential drought and flood risks.

2. What are the benefits?

SpaceGuard Africa provides several important benefits:

  • Environmental monitoring: Combines satellite observations with local ground-based measurements.
  • Trend analysis: Helps identify increasing and decreasing patterns in environmental variables over time.
  • Disaster preparedness: Supports awareness of conditions associated with drought and flooding.
  • Regional coverage: Allows users to explore environmental information for multiple locations, including areas without physical monitoring stations.
  • Accessible information: Presents complex environmental data through an interactive dashboard.
  • Data-driven decisions: Provides useful environmental information for communities, researchers, agricultural stakeholders and disaster-management authorities.

3. Intended impact

Our long-term vision is to strengthen environmental awareness and climate resilience in The Gambia and other African countries.

We want to make environmental information more accessible, particularly for communities that may have limited access to local monitoring infrastructure. By combining NASA observations with ground-level measurements, SpaceGuard Africa aims to support better understanding of environmental changes, improve preparedness and contribute to more informed responses to climate-related risks.

In the future, the platform could be expanded through additional monitoring stations, improved sensor calibration, longer historical datasets, more advanced AI models and connections with relevant environmental and disaster-management institutions.

4. Tools, technologies and resources used

Our project combines hardware engineering, software development, cloud technologies and Earth science data.

Hardware and electronics

  • Arduino MKR WiFi 1010 microcontroller.
  • DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor.
  • Capacitive soil moisture sensor.
  • Rain detection sensor.
  • Water-level detection sensor.
  • Connecting wires and electronic prototyping components.

Software and development technologies

  • Arduino IDE and Arduino IoT Cloud development environment for microcontroller programming.
  • C/C++ for embedded programming.
  • Python for backend development and environmental data processing.
  • FastAPI for backend API services.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web-based interface.
  • Render for cloud hosting and deployment.
  • Supabase for planned or integrated cloud database services, where applicable.
  • AI-assisted development and analysis tools.

Scientific data

  • NASA Earth observation and climate datasets.
  • NASA POWER environmental data, including precipitation, temperature, relative humidity and wind speed variables.
  • Statistical methods such as Mann-Kendall trend analysis and Sen's slope estimation for investigating environmental trends.

5. What makes the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of SpaceGuard Africa lies in bringing together satellite-based environmental intelligence and an affordable, locally developed physical monitoring station within one platform.

Instead of relying exclusively on satellite observations or individual ground sensors, the project explores how these sources can complement one another. NASA datasets provide broader geographical and historical coverage, while the physical station supplies local measurements that can help provide additional environmental context.

Another innovative aspect is its regional approach. The platform is designed to distinguish between locations with physical monitoring infrastructure and locations where environmental information is obtained from NASA datasets. This allows the system to explore environmental conditions across wider geographical areas without suggesting that every location has a physical station.

The project also incorporates AI-supported interpretation and statistical trend analysis to make environmental information easier to understand and potentially more useful for early-warning applications.

6. Factors considered during development

Our team considered affordability, accessibility, geographical coverage, data availability, connectivity, scalability and practical implementation.

We selected relatively affordable electronic components and a Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller to demonstrate the feasibility of locally developed environmental monitoring stations. We also considered the importance of combining local measurements with established scientific datasets rather than depending on a single source of information.

Data reliability is another important consideration. Raw sensor readings require calibration before they can be interpreted as accurate physical measurements or used in validated risk assessments. Similarly, satellite observations and historical trends must be interpreted carefully, with attention to geographical differences, data limitations and uncertainty.

Ultimately, SpaceGuard Africa is designed as a scalable environmental intelligence initiative that can grow from a working prototype in Fajara into a wider regional monitoring and disaster-preparedness platform.
